\[
R(p) = \max\left(\sum_{x \in S_b} \left(I_x - I_p - t\right),\ \sum_{x \in S_d} \left(I_p - I_x - t\right)\right) \;\text{ if } p \text{ passes the segment test, else } 0
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I_p\): The value at the center
- \(t\): The threshold
- \(S_b, S_d\): The brighter and the darker circle pixels
- \(n\): The run length

The circle holds 16 pixels at radius 3 around p. S_b holds the circle pixels brighter than I_p + t and S_d those darker than I_p - t. The segment test passes when at least n circle pixels in a row are all in S_b or all in S_d. Rosten and Drummond proposed this score for non-maximum suppression. Values are on a 0 to 1 scale. The corners output keeps pixels with a score above 0 that are the largest within the minimum distance. The segment test gives the same corners as skimage.feature.corner_fast, whose score is computed differently.
